messages:
Anya K: quick idea — instead of creating N peering connections for control-plane VPCs, what if we build a microsegmented control plane over a Transit Gateway? fewer attachments, central routing, per-tenant policy via route tables / prefix-lists. pros/cons? :thinking_face:
Devon R: sounds interesting. can you clarify "microsegmented" — separate route tables per tenant and attach security policies?
Anya K: yep — each tenant gets a scoped route table + prefix-list that only allows its dataplane subnet ranges to reach controlplane endpoints. controlplane services still run in multiple AZs, but the TGW enforces lateral boundaries.
Sahil P: watch route table limits. TGW route table associations/propagations scale but aren't infinite. also need to consider number of attachments per TGW and per-account quotas.
Maria G: cross-account attachments + IAM roles will get messy. we'll need a clear account-owner mapping and automation for acceptance flows. also flow logs + VPC logs will now converge into fewer places — good for visibility, but ops needs filtering.
Patrick L: latency/cost note — hairpinning through TGW can introduce hop + inter-AZ data charges. If we proxy controlplane traffic back through TGW instead of local peering, we might induce SNAT on some setups. how do we preserve source IPs?
Anya K: good point. preserving client IP is important for audit and some features. we can 1) terminate TLS at edge and pass X-Forwarded-For, 2) use proxy protocol, or 3) keep a small set of direct peering links for customers that require true source preservation.
Devon R: hybrid model = TGW for most tenants, direct VPC peering for VIPs. gives us lower churn but lets customers with strict IP requirements avoid proxy paths.
Sahil P: also consider prefix-lists to avoid full route duplication. instead of per-tenant explicit routes, group tenants by CIDR blocks with prefix-lists and use route table entries that reference those lists. reduces number of entries but still enforces segmentation.
Maria G: cert rotation + mTLS question: if controlplane endpoints are consolidated, cert distribution becomes simpler but rotation blast radius grows. we need per-tenant identity in certs or a short-lived cert model and strong revocation/issuer flow.
Patrick L: operational failure mode: TGW route table mis-association could blackhole a tenant. we need automated reconciliation and a safe default route that fails to a local HA proxy rather than blackhole.
infra-bot: quick estimate: spike with TGW + 50 attachments will add ~X$/month in TGW processing + X$/GB transit in naive model (prod numbers to be clarified).
Anya K: ok concrete tradeoffs summary: fewer peer objects vs more complex TGW config + potential latency/cost. stronger central policy, but larger blast radius and quota surface.
Devon R: propose spike: implement TGW control plane in a new sandbox org with 50 synthetic tenants, test attachment churn, route table scaling, and source-ip preservation patterns. measure RTT and token auth latency.
Maria G: I'll take IAM + flow logs automation for the spike — generate acceptance automation and a CI job to validate attachment policies.
Sahil P: I'll own route table / prefix-list spike and validate association limits and propagation behavior.
Patrick L: I'll test proxy options for maintaining source identity (proxy-protocol, XFF, eBPF passthrough test).
Anya K: timeline: 2 weeks spike. deliverables: cost model, latency numbers, attack/failure modes doc, and recommended rollout plan (hybrid or full TGW). owners: @Devon R, @Maria G, @Sahil P, @Patrick L.
Devon R: SGTM. I'll open the spike ticket and link here.
ops-bot: FYI — please add these changes to the change calendar if spike requires infra quota increases.
Anya K: thanks team. if we see route table scaling issues we fallback to per-tenant small VPC peering + aggregated routes. will post spike plan in a separate thread with diagrams. :thumbsup:
